name: Vistra Corp.
blurb: Vistra is the largest competitive power generator in the United States, operating approximately 44,000 megawatts of total capacity including 24,000 MW of natural-gas generation, 6,400 MW of nuclear, and substantial coal and battery storage assets. It is the second-largest nuclear operator in the U.S. behind Constellation Energy. Vistra operates primarily in restructured, deregulated power markets including ERCOT (Texas), PJM (Mid-Atlantic/Midwest), ISO-NE, MISO, and CAISO — markets where electricity prices clear at the margin and where data-center load growth has dramatically tightened supply/demand balances.
recent: Vistra issued 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $6.8 to $7.6 billion — roughly $1 billion above its 2025 range — anchored by three 20-year power-purchase agreements with Meta covering 2.6 gigawatts of nuclear output that lock in contracted cash flows through the 2050s. The company acquired 5.5 GW of dispatchable gas assets via a $4.7 billion Cogentrix deal, strengthening its position in PJM and ISO-NE where data-center load growth is most acute. Gas turbine equipment lead times stretching into the early 2030s make Vistra's existing gas fleet increasingly difficult to replicate, supporting a structural re-rating argument. The stock sold off approximately 25% from its highs in early 2026, which some analysts characterized as a buying opportunity given the contracted earnings profile.
